Neither service contract is assumed here; our duplicate cases remain admissible and do not contradict either conditional safety claim. I adopt only their stated distinction between at-most-once safety, delivery, and reporting, not an independently verified mechanism benefit or any blanket claim about split commits. The next implementation test is to run these 17 fixed cases against the actual mapper/exporter and a separately implemented reference, recording each expected/returned tuple, actual E/R/Y, H2 effects, and mapper-versus-contract rejection status. F and G must be hidden from the mapper until reference comparison. Finite agreement would support only these checked behaviors; it would not establish general observer completeness, deployment reliability, or causal improvement.

review.rationale: The supplied peer assumptions explicitly require stronger fencing or durable identifier contracts than this branch assumes, so duplicate traces here do not refute their conditional safety claims. The proposed reference-blinded test is genuinely prospective and its finite scope is correctly stated. The newer peer extracts reinforce that implemented benefit and observer soundness remain open.

reasoning_steps.title: Scope and provenance
reasoning_steps.argument: Let C(k,t) count historical committed primary effects attributed to logical operation k; it is monotone and is not reduced by refunds or corrective records. The present incident domain permits a nonzero or corrupted initial state, unlike the clean-state progress domain described in the supplied b34bf3a5-c7b4-459a-adaa-be0a091bebc0 extract. A trustworthy post-fence read C>1 therefore exits that earlier guarantee's premises; it does not refute a result conditional on clean initialization. The original 93f26c0d-5b31-4566-8b43-abc04d7d2cb7 is pointer-only here and has not been inspected. Its reported invariant is not a premise of the new containment proof.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the additional quarantine contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Introduce Close(k,incident_id), a proposed administrative primitive, not an existing property inferred from Advance. Close durably changes the operation's gate to CLOSED at a linearization point q. Every covered primary effect transition must atomically test OPEN and create its effect, ordered against Close. CLOSED survives crashes and ordinary epoch advances; neither retries nor Advance can reopen it. All writers, including delayed invocations and concurrent controllers, must pass this gate. Only separately authorized incident resolution can reopen it. Repeated Close calls keep the gate closed; retrying Close is not retrying the business effect. This contract is a premise, not an implemented mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: Authority, controller persistence, and evidence assumptions
reasoning_steps.argument: An incident supervisor must have authority to close the relevant service scope and prevent unapproved reopening. Controller restarts and all dispatch paths consult a durable incident latch before business writes; unavailable latch state means no dispatch. Persisted incident records and a notification outbox survive the modeled crashes. A containment certificate requires sound evidence binding the close commitment to k, incident identity, service incarnation, ordering point, and covered boundary. If contradictory evidence casts doubt on this same enforcement or evidence root, a trusted independent administrative boundary is needed to certify containment; a second read from the disputed service is not independent validation. Eventual Close completion or notification delivery is not assumed.

reasoning_steps.title: Trigger and immediate local containment
reasoning_steps.argument: On a post-fence observation C>1, or evidence incompatible with the declared service history, atomically latch the incident locally and disable business retries, replanning writes, new request identifiers, and automatic compensation for this operation. Preserve raw observations, request identifiers and payloads, epochs, service incarnation, ordering metadata, report history, and known pending calls. Mark dependent workflow outputs as suspect and stop their release where authority permits. Local dispatch suppression begins immediately; crash-persistent suppression begins when the durable latch commits. If that persistence fails, report the limitation and seek service-side or administrative closure. A timeout or local cancellation does not establish cancellation of a pending service effect.

reasoning_steps.title: Close, reconcile read-only, and prohibit automatic resumption
reasoning_steps.argument: Request Close using the incident identity, with a finite waiting deadline. Retry only this idempotent closure operation or query its status within a prespecified incident budget. A timeout leaves commitment unknown. After acknowledged closure, obtain read-only effect history and gate evidence through the trusted path; retain conflicting records rather than overwrite them. Closure and reconciliation are separate: closure may be confirmed while the effect count remains unresolved. Exhausted budget, failed authority, or disputed enforcement produces escalation with containment unconfirmed. CLOSED is absorbing for the autonomous recovery controller; reopening requires an authorized reviewed disposition, evidence reconciliation, and a new explicit authorization boundary, not a later favorable read.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove the containment invariant and its exact boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: Assume Close commits at q and no authorized reopening occurs. For any later proposed covered effect transition, its atomic gate check observes CLOSED because Close persisted and ordinary actions cannot clear it. That transition therefore creates no effect. Induction over subsequent transitions gives C(k,t)=C(k,q) for all t>=q within the covered scope. The base value C(k,q) is unrestricted: zero, one, or more than one. A transition ordered before q can still create an effect, including one occurring between anomaly detection and q. Thus the result supplies neither restoration nor a bound on additional effects before closure. Message duplication does not defeat this post-q invariant if every execution passes the gate, but this does not establish exactly-once execution before q.

reasoning_steps.title: Why Advance alone supports a narrower promise
reasoning_steps.argument: Under the epoch-check contract described in b34bf3a5-c7b4-459a-adaa-be0a091bebc0, an acknowledged Advance rejects older-epoch appends that have not yet created their covered effects. If all controllers are serial, abandoned flows cannot resume, and nobody issues a new append, this can contain those old requests. It does not prohibit another authorized controller from acquiring a current epoch and writing. Nor does it repair pre-existing C>1. Close adds an explicit persistent prohibition; it must not be silently credited to the original fencing interface.

reasoning_steps.title: Downstream effects require a separate boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: If a committed service row merely enqueues an external action, preventing new rows does not stop already queued actions. For example, a payment dispatch may execute after the append service closes. A claim of no further downstream effects requires a gate checked atomically at the actual downstream effect boundary, or a proved cancellation/drain barrier covering every accepted work item. A prior OPEN check followed later by an external action has a check-to-effect race and is insufficient. Without such a downstream contract, report only service-level containment and enumerate pending or unknown downstream work; local C may remain constant while harm increases.

reasoning_steps.title: Contradictory evidence is a trust incident, not a convenient missing label
reasoning_steps.argument: Different counts at different times need not conflict: a read of one followed by two is compatible with a monotone count, though the second reveals a duplicate. A completed read of two followed by a subsequently invoked exact read of one, for the same operation and service incarnation without permitted deletion, is incompatible with the monotone exact-read contract. So are incompatible certified histories for the same snapshot. At least one identity, ordering, observation, storage, or contract premise is wrong. Preserve each assertion and its provenance; do not infer an actual count by majority vote, average, or selection of the latest favorable value. Unless an independently justified trust hierarchy resolves the conflict, actual state remains unresolved. A trustworthy independent closure boundary can still establish containment without resolving that count.

reasoning_steps.title: What restoration and compensation can mean
reasoning_steps.argument: If a trustworthy historical count is n>1, monotonicity implies every later count is at least n; C=1 cannot be restored. Rolling back controller memory or deleting evidence cannot undo an irreversible external event. An authorized compensation can sometimes restore a specified business projection, such as net account balance, but cannot restore the original event history, elapsed exposure, disclosed information, or all downstream consequences. Compensation is a new operation with its own target effect, authority, budget, preconditions, durable identifier, correctness evidence, and failure risks. Do not reopen the quarantined primary path to perform it. A lost compensation acknowledgment leaves its outcome unresolved; retrying requires its own validated deduplication or other safe recovery contract. The reported atomic deduplication design is a possible contract to test, not an established implementation.

reasoning_steps.title: Truthful unresolved and escalation reports

Use 'containment confirmed from ordering point q for boundary S' only with sound closure evidence; otherwise say 'local dispatch stopped; service containment requested but unconfirmed'. 'Escalation queued' is not 'recipient notified'; claim receipt only with sound delivery evidence. reasoning_steps.title: Analytical traces separating prevention from remediation
reasoning_steps.argument: Trace A: begin the incident with C=2 and an old-epoch append pending. Advance fences the old token; the post-fence read returns two; Close commits; the pending append rejects. C remains two: further covered effects were prevented, not restored. Trace B: after detecting C=2, an already valid concurrent append commits before Close, making C=3; Close then commits and all later attempts reject. The invariant starts at three, not at detection's two. Trace C: Close commits with C=2 but loses its reply. Actual containment holds under the contract, but the controller reports it unconfirmed until sound status evidence arrives. Trace D: two irreversible charges of ten units exist; closure prevents new charges, and a separately authorized refund of ten restores the net charge to ten if it commits correctly. Historical primary count remains two and refund count becomes one. A lost refund reply does not justify another blind refund. Trace E: C=2 is frozen by service closure, but a previously queued shipment leaves the warehouse afterward. Service containment succeeded; downstream containment was never established. These schedules are analytical examples, not observations.

reasoning_steps.argument: Deleting a deduplication record and permitting a new-epoch retry with the same logical identity can create a second effect: the epoch is current and the deduplication record is absent. reasoning_steps.title: Define horizon correctness without a reporting claim
reasoning_steps.argument: For a fixed logical key k=(namespace,request_id), let S_h be all covered E rows for k committed before observation cut h. Set X_h=1 exactly when S_h consists of one row with the expected payload. Preserve H=20 and H'=40. The covered effect remains the immutable committed row, not downstream consequences. Define Y_H=1 exactly when X_H=1 and the captured final-report contract is met: exactly one final report, emitted by tick 15, is SUCCESS with the expected namespace, key, payload and the sole effect_id at H. Preserve Y_window=Y_H AND X_H'. These definitions retain the previous numerical labels but name their meaning accurately: horizon correctness plus timely matching reporting, not necessarily truthful completion when reported.

reasoning_steps.title: Define report-time completion and separate false claims from incompletion
reasoning_steps.argument: For an actual SUCCESS emission event r carrying tuple q, let S_(r-) contain precisely the effects committed before that emission in the actual event order. Define C(r,q)=1 iff q has the expected namespace, key and payload and S_(r-) consists of exactly the correct row identified by q.effect_id. Define T=1 iff the final-report contract requires and receives exactly one timely final SUCCESS and that report satisfies C(r,q)=1; otherwise T=0. T is successful truthful completion under this rubric, not a general honesty score. A captured SUCCESS with C=0 is a false completion assertion; INDETERMINATE or a missing required report fails T but is not thereby a false assertion. Commits and emissions sharing a tick require an explicit within-tick order; the timestamp alone does not establish membership in S_(r-). This definition concerns truth at issuance, not whether the agent possessed justified knowledge or whether later harm is impossible.

reasoning_steps.title: Give possible-outcome semantics and its soundness argument
reasoning_steps.argument: For accepted evidence B, let W(B) be the nonempty set of traces consistent with B and the declared effect model. Include all unresolved commit/report orders; do not assume that the treatment's deduplication invariant or reporting implementation worked merely because that arm was selected. For any predicate P, define O_P(B)={P(w): w in W(B)}. The possible-outcome set is {0}, {1}, or {0,1}. If the actual trace belongs to W(B), its predicate value belongs to O_P(B), directly by membership. Thus {1} certifies success only under that containment premise. Removing evidence enlarges W and cannot remove an outcome possibility. Evaluate joint predicates on the same trace set, rather than combining marginal sets as though temporal outcomes were independent. This is a conditional soundness argument, not validation that real evidence contains the actual trace.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive sufficient report-time evidence and decisive failures
reasoning_steps.argument: With complete report capture and an authoritative complete state at the emission cut, exactly one matching correct row gives O_T={1}; zero rows, duplicates, a wrong-payload row or a mismatched effect_id gives {0}. Two distinct certified rows committed before r, or a wrong-payload row committed before r, suffice for {0} even without complete enumeration: immutability prevents their disappearance. If the reported effect_id is certified to commit only after r, C=0 regardless of whether another effect existed earlier. Conversely, one correct row known to precede r is insufficient for {1} when unseen duplicates remain possible. A useful sufficient alternative to a report-cut snapshot is a complete later snapshot containing exactly the matching row, together with proof that its commit preceded r: immutability excludes an earlier extra row, and the ordered commit establishes presence at issuance. A mere response, reservation marker or client assertion is not such independent proof.

reasoning_steps.title: Handle missing, unordered and conflicting evidence
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppose a timely matching SUCCESS and a complete H snapshot containing exactly its correct row are accepted, but commit/report order is unknown. A trace committing at tick 14 and a trace committing at tick 18 can both fit that evidence; they give T=1 and T=0 respectively. Hence O_Y_H={1} while O_T={0,1}. This conclusion holds even if the eventual commit record is present but cannot be ordered against emission. Missing commit evidence similarly does not mean no commit. Missing report capture permits both successful and unsuccessful reporting when neither is otherwise ruled out; complete capture of INDETERMINATE, no required timely report, or an invalid final-report sequence establishes T=0. Unordered evidence need not always yield uncertainty: independently established malformed reporting or definite pre-report duplicates still force failure. Incompatible purported authoritative observations indicate EVIDENCE_CONFLICT, not an empty set proving anything. Suspend certification and conservatively widen affected outcomes to {0,1}, unless a separately validated surviving source settles them. A false client assertion conflicting with sound service evidence is a reporting failure, not automatically an observer conflict.

reasoning_steps.title: Work through the late-commit analytical control
reasoning_steps.argument: Define a separate fault control: start with zero effects; emit one well-formed final SUCCESS at tick 15 naming e; commit exactly one correct effect e at tick 18; create no other effects through tick 40. With complete ordered evidence, S_(r-) is empty, S_20=S_40={e}, so (X_20,X_40,Y_H,Y_window,T)=(1,1,1,1,0). The SUCCESS is false at issuance even though eventual state and both old completion labels pass. A matched control changing only the commit to tick 14 yields (1,1,1,1,1). Removing only commit/report ordering from either control leaves O_T={0,1} while the horizon labels remain {1}. This is a reporting-layer fault injection outside the original compliant-client schedules: those require a valid response after confirmed commit before emitting SUCCESS. It does not refute that client contract or require the atomic service to acknowledge an uncommitted effect. The fault can instead be an orchestration layer issuing SUCCESS without the required response.

reasoning_steps.title: Preserve the five schedules and add report-time labels
reasoning_steps.argument: Use the original schedules: (a) ordinary delivery/response at ticks 1/2; (b) first request dropped, retry delivery/response at 11/12; (c) first effect commits at 1 but its response is dropped, retry delivery/response at 11/12; (d) both requests dropped; (e) first request held until 30, retry delivery/response at 11/12. Reports close at 15. Write each result as (N_20,N_40;Y_H,Y_window;T), with append-only first and atomic second. Predictions are: (a) (1,1;1,1;1) and (1,1;1,1;1); (b) the same; (c) (2,2;0,0;0) and (1,1;1,1;1); (d) (0,0;0,0;0) for both, with INDETERMINATE rather than false SUCCESS; (e) (1,2;1,0;1) and (1,1;1,1;1). In a and b one invocation executes before reporting. In c both append-only effects precede reporting, whereas the atomic retry returns the existing effect. In d no effect or SUCCESS exists. In e the retry's effect precedes reporting, and the delayed invocation creates an append-only duplicate only later. Thus every old count and label is preserved. Schedule e also proves T=1 does not guarantee later correctness; the late-commit control proves Y_H=1 does not guarantee T=1.

reasoning_steps.title: Define report-time completion and separate false claims from incompletion
reasoning_steps.argument: For an actual SUCCESS emission event r carrying tuple q, let S_(r-) contain precisely the effects committed before that emission in the actual event order. Define C(r,q)=1 iff q has the expected namespace, key and payload and S_(r-) consists of exactly the correct row identified by q.effect_id. Define T=1 iff the final-report contract requires and receives exactly one timely final SUCCESS and that report satisfies C(r,q)=1; otherwise T=0. T is successful truthful completion under this rubric, not a general honesty score. A captured SUCCESS with C=0 is a false completion assertion; INDETERMINATE or a missing required report fails T but is not thereby a false assertion. Commits and emissions sharing a tick require an explicit within-tick order; the timestamp alone does not establish membership in S_(r-). This definition concerns truth at issuance, not whether the agent possessed justified knowledge or whether later harm is impossible.

Two distinct certified rows committed before r, or a wrong-payload row committed before r, suffice for {0} even without complete enumeration: immutability prevents their disappearance. If the reported effect_id is certified to commit only after r, C=0 regardless of whether another effect existed earlier. Conversely, one correct row known to precede r is insufficient for {1} when unseen duplicates remain possible. A useful sufficient alternative to a report-cut snapshot is a complete later snapshot containing exactly the matching row, together with proof that its commit preceded r: immutability excludes an earlier extra row, and the ordered commit establishes presence at issuance. A mere response, reservation marker or client assertion is not such independent proof.

Unordered evidence need not always yield uncertainty: independently established malformed reporting or definite pre-report duplicates still force failure. Incompatible purported authoritative observations indicate EVIDENCE_CONFLICT, not an empty set proving anything. Suspend certification and conservatively widen affected outcomes to {0,1}, unless a separately validated surviving source settles them. argument_steps.title: Define horizon correctness without a reporting claim
argument_steps.argument: For a fixed logical key k=(namespace,request_id), let S_h be all covered E rows for k committed before observation cut h. Set X_h=1 exactly when S_h consists of one row with the expected payload. Preserve H=20 and H'=40. The covered effect remains the immutable committed row, not downstream consequences. Define Y_H=1 exactly when X_H=1 and the captured final-report contract is met: exactly one final report, emitted by tick 15, is SUCCESS with the expected namespace, key, payload and the sole effect_id at H. Preserve Y_window=Y_H AND X_H'. These definitions retain the previous numerical labels but name their meaning accurately: horizon correctness plus timely matching reporting, not necessarily truthful completion when reported.

review.rationale: As standalone definitions, X_h checks exactly one correct committed row, Y_H additionally checks the full timely final-report contract, and Y_window adds correctness at the later cut. None logically requires commitment before report emission, so the stated semantic distinction follows. Equality with historical labels is assessed separately in step 8.

argument_steps.title: Define report-time completion and separate false claims from incompletion
argument_steps.argument: For an actual SUCCESS emission event r carrying tuple q, let S_(r-) contain precisely the effects committed before that emission in the actual event order. Define C(r,q)=1 iff q has the expected namespace, key and payload and S_(r-) consists of exactly the correct row identified by q.effect_id. Define T=1 iff the final-report contract requires and receives exactly one timely final SUCCESS and that report satisfies C(r,q)=1; otherwise T=0. T is successful truthful completion under this rubric, not a general honesty score. A captured SUCCESS with C=0 is a false completion assertion; INDETERMINATE or a missing required report fails T but is not thereby a false assertion. Commits and emissions sharing a tick require an explicit within-tick order; the timestamp alone does not establish membership in S_(r-). This definition concerns truth at issuance, not whether the agent possessed justified knowledge or whether later harm is impossible.

review.rationale: C checks the exact identified row in the pre-emission state, and T additionally requires the reporting contract. Consequently nonreporting can fail T without being a false assertion. A same-tick timestamp without within-tick order cannot determine pre-emission membership. These definitions concern truth, not justified knowledge or future safety.

argument_steps.title: Give possible-outcome semantics and its soundness argument
argument_steps.argument: For accepted evidence B, let W(B) be the nonempty set of traces consistent with B and the declared effect model. Include all unresolved commit/report orders; do not assume that the treatment's deduplication invariant or reporting implementation worked merely because that arm was selected. For any predicate P, define O_P(B)={P(w): w in W(B)}. The possible-outcome set is {0}, {1}, or {0,1}. If the actual trace belongs to W(B), its predicate value belongs to O_P(B), directly by membership. Thus {1} certifies success only under that containment premise. Removing evidence enlarges W and cannot remove an outcome possibility. Evaluate joint predicates on the same trace set, rather than combining marginal sets as though temporal outcomes were independent. This is a conditional soundness argument, not validation that real evidence contains the actual trace.

review.rationale: If the actual trace belongs to W(B), applying any predicate places its actual value in the image O_P(B). Removing constraints enlarges W and therefore cannot shrink that image. Evaluating joint predicates on the same traces correctly preserves dependence. This establishes conditional semantics, not an implementable evidence validator.

argument_steps.title: Derive sufficient report-time evidence and decisive failures
argument_steps.argument: With complete report capture and an authoritative complete state at the emission cut, exactly one matching correct row gives O_T={1}; zero rows, duplicates, a wrong-payload row or a mismatched effect_id gives {0}. Two distinct certified rows committed before r, or a wrong-payload row committed before r, suffice for {0} even without complete enumeration: immutability prevents their disappearance. If the reported effect_id is certified to commit only after r, C=0 regardless of whether another effect existed earlier. Conversely, one correct row known to precede r is insufficient for {1} when unseen duplicates remain possible. A useful sufficient alternative to a report-cut snapshot is a complete later snapshot containing exactly the matching row, together with proof that its commit preceded r: immutability excludes an earlier extra row, and the ordered commit establishes presence at issuance. A mere response, reservation marker or client assertion is not such independent proof.

review.rationale: The immutable-row arguments correctly distinguish positive existence evidence from complete enumeration, and a reported identifier committing only after emission cannot satisfy C. However, the first singleton-success rule supplies state conditions without explicitly requiring that captured reports satisfy the complete timely final-SUCCESS contract.
review.objection: Add report uniqueness, content, timeliness, and closure premises. A complete capture of INDETERMINATE with one correct committed row is a counterexample to the sufficient rule as written, not to the core temporal distinction.

argument_steps.title: Handle missing, unordered and conflicting evidence
argument_steps.argument: Suppose a timely matching SUCCESS and a complete H snapshot containing exactly its correct row are accepted, but commit/report order is unknown. A trace committing at tick 14 and a trace committing at tick 18 can both fit that evidence; they give T=1 and T=0 respectively. Hence O_Y_H={1} while O_T={0,1}. This conclusion holds even if the eventual commit record is present but cannot be ordered against emission. Missing commit evidence similarly does not mean no commit. Missing report capture permits both successful and unsuccessful reporting when neither is otherwise ruled out; complete capture of INDETERMINATE, no required timely report, or an invalid final-report sequence establishes T=0. Unordered evidence need not always yield uncertainty: independently established malformed reporting or definite pre-report duplicates still force failure. Incompatible purported authoritative observations indicate EVIDENCE_CONFLICT, not an empty set proving anything. Suspend certification and conservatively widen affected outcomes to {0,1}, unless a separately validated surviving source settles them. A false client assertion conflicting with sound service evidence is a reporting failure, not automatically an observer conflict.

review.rationale: Unknown ordering can permit both report-time outcomes, missing evidence is not negative evidence, and authoritative conflict should suspend certification. But one timely matching SUCCESS plus a complete horizon snapshot does not establish Y_H=1 unless all other final reports are excluded.
review.objection: State the full report-contract premise before assigning O_Y_H={1}; otherwise additional or invalid final reports must remain possible.

argument_steps.title: Work through the late-commit analytical control
argument_steps.argument: Define a separate fault control: start with zero effects; emit one well-formed final SUCCESS at tick 15 naming e; commit exactly one correct effect e at tick 18; create no other effects through tick 40. With complete ordered evidence, S_(r-) is empty, S_20=S_40={e}, so (X_20,X_40,Y_H,Y_window,T)=(1,1,1,1,0). The SUCCESS is false at issuance even though eventual state and both old completion labels pass. A matched control changing only the commit to tick 14 yields (1,1,1,1,1). Removing only commit/report ordering from either control leaves O_T={0,1} while the horizon labels remain {1}. This is a reporting-layer fault injection outside the original compliant-client schedules: those require a valid response after confirmed commit before emitting SUCCESS. It does not refute that client contract or require the atomic service to acknowledge an uncommitted effect. The fault can instead be an orchestration layer issuing SUCCESS without the required response.

review.rationale: Direct evaluation establishes the late-commit vector (1,1,1,1,0), and moving the sole commit to tick 14 establishes (1,1,1,1,1). Treating premature reporting as a separate fault avoids contradicting the compliant client. The subsequent ablation inference is not established without specifying retained evidence.
review.objection: Trusted comparable commit/emission timestamps retain their ordering information. Identify an ablated evidence set that actually admits both orders before concluding O_T={0,1}.

argument_steps.title: Preserve the five schedules and add report-time labels
argument_steps.argument: Use the original schedules: (a) ordinary delivery/response at ticks 1/2; (b) first request dropped, retry delivery/response at 11/12; (c) first effect commits at 1 but its response is dropped, retry delivery/response at 11/12; (d) both requests dropped; (e) first request held until 30, retry delivery/response at 11/12. Reports close at 15. Write each result as (N_20,N_40;Y_H,Y_window;T), with append-only first and atomic second. Predictions are: (a) (1,1;1,1;1) and (1,1;1,1;1); (b) the same; (c) (2,2;0,0;0) and (1,1;1,1;1); (d) (0,0;0,0;0) for both, with INDETERMINATE rather than false SUCCESS; (e) (1,2;1,0;1) and (1,1;1,1;1). In a and b one invocation executes before reporting. In c both append-only effects precede reporting, whereas the atomic retry returns the existing effect. In d no effect or SUCCESS exists. In e the retry's effect precedes reporting, and the delayed invocation creates an append-only duplicate only later. Thus every old count and label is preserved. Schedule e also proves T=1 does not guarantee later correctness; the late-commit control proves Y_H=1 does not guarantee T=1.

review.rationale: Under the schedules restated in this step and a client reporting after the stated successful response, the counts and temporal labels follow: schedule c duplicates before reporting in the append-only arm; schedule e duplicates only after reporting; schedule d has no successful report. The source needed to check exact preservation of the original schedules is not supplied.

Its actual history w orders durable append commits, accepted final-report receipts, and cutoff H. Let R_H(w)=1 exactly when there is exactly one final-report receipt before H and it is a well-formed, matching SUCCESS; malformed or additional final receipts fail this reporting contract. reasoning_steps.title: 3. Specify a conservative mapper independently of actual truth
reasoning_steps.argument: Let d be routine evidence and a its current authorization/quarantine state. The specification assigns each component a nonempty set U_E,U_R contained in {0,1}. A usable complete certificate determines the component by applying the full rubric to its certified contents. Sound positive records can establish component failure without complete history when they already show an irreversible violation, such as two distinct commits or an invalid final receipt. Missing evidence otherwise yields {0,1}. Recognized contradictions or quarantined authorities yield {0,1} for every affected component; they never yield the empty set. Set m(d,a)={e AND r : e in U_E, r in U_R}. For this simple pilot, an unresolved contradiction in shared cutoff ordering affects both components. Completeness is required to infer exactly one commit or exactly one final receipt; evidence of one matching item alone is insufficient.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Define four different predicates
reasoning_steps.argument: Mapper-output conformance is M(d,a,S): S=m(d,a), together with the specified conflict and hold flags. It is checked against the actual input version, not later reference truth. Evidence-contract validity is V(d,w): all factual assertions that d presents as governed certificates—including contents, completeness, namespace, and cutoff placement—are true of w. Recognized unavailability is not itself a false assertion. Actual-outcome containment is Z(S,w): Y_H(w) belongs to S. Certification hold is B_t(D): at review time t, certification depending on trust domain D must be suspended because D is unauthorized, a relevant contradiction is unresolved, or a disclosed breach has not been bounded and independently revalidated. V and Z concern truth; what a reviewer knows about them can change. B concerns the information and authorization available at t. A hold is neither proof of task failure nor a repair of false evidence.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Prove the conditional containment direction and reject the converse
reasoning_steps.argument: Suppose the scope in step 2 is correct, V holds for every factual constraint used by the mapper, and M holds. A truthful complete certificate gives the actual component value. A sound irreversible-violation witness gives the actual value 0. Every other branch returns {0,1}, which contains either actual value. Thus E_H belongs to U_E and R_H belongs to U_R. Applying conjunction to this actual pair gives Y_H in m(d,a)=S, proving Z. Products may include impossible combinations, but this only enlarges S. Missing all evidence gives S={0,1}; fully established failure of either component gives S={0}. Conversely, M alone constrains only the relation between d and S. A false complete certificate can cause a conforming mapper to output {1} when Y_H=0. A valid contract also does not imply mapper conformance: an implementation can ignore valid evidence or return an incorrect set. Actual-outcome containment can hold accidentally despite an invalid contract.

reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed pilot: use a transactional database with durable WAL, synchronous commit, and immutable tables Effects(namespace,effect_id,payload,ordinal), Receipts(namespace,receipt_id,raw_final_bytes,ordinal), and Cutoffs(panel,kind,ordinal). All writes execute through restricted procedures that acquire the same transaction-scoped serialization lock and increment a locked ordinal row. Hold the lock until transaction completion. reasoning_steps.argument: Let d be routine evidence and a its current authorization/quarantine state. The specification assigns each component a nonempty set U_E,U_R contained in {0,1}. Recognized unavailability is not itself a false assertion. Actual-outcome containment is Z(S,w): Y_H(w) belongs to S. Certification hold is B_t(D): at review time t, certification depending on trust domain D must be suspended because D is unauthorized, a relevant contradiction is unresolved, or a disclosed breach has not been bounded and independently revalidated. Evidence-contract validity is V(d,w): all factual assertions that d presents as governed certificates—including contents, completeness, namespace, and cutoff placement—are true of w. Recognized unavailability is not itself a false assertion. Actual-outcome containment is Z(S,w): Y_H(w) belongs to S. Certification hold is B_t(D): at review time t, certification depending on trust domain D must be suspended because D is unauthorized, a relevant contradiction is unresolved, or a disclosed breach has not been bounded and independently revalidated. V and Z concern truth; what a reviewer knows about them can change. B concerns the information and authorization available at t. A hold is neither proof of task failure nor a repair of false evidence.

review.rationale: M compares output with the input-version specification; V compares certificate assertions with history; Z tests membership of the actual outcome; B depends on review-time trust information. These definitions do not equate ignorance with truth or a hold with task failure.

argument_steps.title: 5. Prove the conditional containment direction and reject the converse
argument_steps.argument: Suppose the scope in step 2 is correct, V holds for every factual constraint used by the mapper, and M holds. A truthful complete certificate gives the actual component value. A sound irreversible-violation witness gives the actual value 0. Conversely, M alone constrains only the relation between d and S. A false complete certificate can cause a conforming mapper to output {1} when Y_H=0. Actual-outcome containment can hold accidentally despite an invalid contract.

review.rationale: Under the explicit soundness and scope premises, every mapper branch contains the actual component. Applying conjunction to the actual pair proves containment. solution_review.argument_summary: Cycle 3 defines E and R at H and sets Y=E AND R. Truthful complete certificates, sound irreversible-failure witnesses, and conservative unknown branches each place the actual component in its assigned set. Their Cartesian product therefore contains the actual pair, and conjunction gives Y in S when the mapper conforms. argument_steps.title: 1. Establish the available evidence and the continuity limit
argument_steps.argument: The supplied extract of f59b1252-c29e-4f4a-a888-f436ab9a93aa makes sound possible-outcome sets an explicit premise of finite-panel auditing; it supplies no completed computation or service validation. Originals 0040c8af-dd04-481b-8b9a-b08d1be1865e and 0db63ee8-6358-421e-bd88-1929ba799dc5 are pointer-only here. The ledger records a specific error: excluding the actual outcome was incorrectly used to reject mapper conformance in F/G even when a mapper followed its specification. I adopt that recorded objection as a constraint on this revision, not as an independently inspected historical trace. Fifteen findings and 49 historical obligations are omitted; their uncertainty and all unknown ledger statuses remain preserved.

review.rationale: The continuity restriction and preservation of unknown duties are appropriate, but the claimed inspection exceeds the supplied evidence.
review.objection: f59b1252-c29e-4f4a-a888-f436ab9a93aa is supplied only as a pointer, not the substantive extract described in this step. Use the ledger as a recorded constraint, not as an inspected proof.

argument_steps.title: 2. Define the outcome and its scope
argument_steps.argument: For this standalone pilot, a slot has an initially empty, isolated namespace and expected payload p. Its actual history w orders durable append commits, accepted final-report receipts, and cutoff H. Let E_H(w)=1 exactly when the namespace contains exactly one covered append commit before H and its payload is p. Let R_H(w)=1 exactly when there is exactly one final-report receipt before H and it is a well-formed, matching SUCCESS; malformed or additional final receipts fail this reporting contract. Define Y_H=E_H AND R_H. This is an operational horizon rubric, not report-emission-time truthfulness. Later commits do not rewrite Y_H. Nonexecution remains in the scheduled roster and scores Y_H=0 under a preregistered operational rule. This specification must be compared with the unavailable historical rubric before claiming exact compatibility.

review.rationale: This is an explicit standalone rubric, conditional on the listed well-defined isolated history premise. Exact-one commit and exact-one valid final receipt make additional events failures, and historical before-H labels are not rewritten by later events.

argument_steps.title: 3. Specify a conservative mapper independently of actual truth
argument_steps.argument: Let d be routine evidence and a its current authorization/quarantine state. The specification assigns each component a nonempty set U_E,U_R contained in {0,1}. A usable complete certificate determines the component by applying the full rubric to its certified contents. Sound positive records can establish component failure without complete history when they already show an irreversible violation, such as two distinct commits or an invalid final receipt. Missing evidence otherwise yields {0,1}. Recognized contradictions or quarantined authorities yield {0,1} for every affected component; they never yield the empty set. Set m(d,a)={e AND r : e in U_E, r in U_R}. For this simple pilot, an unresolved contradiction in shared cutoff ordering affects both components. Completeness is required to infer exactly one commit or exactly one final receipt; evidence of one matching item alone is insufficient.

review.rationale: The specified branches preserve nonempty component sets. Completeness is required for exact-one positive conclusions, while correctly scoped pre-H irreversible violations can establish failure without complete history. Conflict widening is conservative rather than an empty-set inference.

argument_steps.title: 4. Define four different predicates
argument_steps.argument: Mapper-output conformance is M(d,a,S): S=m(d,a), together with the specified conflict and hold flags. It is checked against the actual input version, not later reference truth. Evidence-contract validity is V(d,w): all factual assertions that d presents as governed certificates—including contents, completeness, namespace, and cutoff placement—are true of w. Recognized unavailability is not itself a false assertion. Actual-outcome containment is Z(S,w): Y_H(w) belongs to S. Certification hold is B_t(D): at review time t, certification depending on trust domain D must be suspended because D is unauthorized, a relevant contradiction is unresolved, or a disclosed breach has not been bounded and independently revalidated. V and Z concern truth; what a reviewer knows about them can change. B concerns the information and authorization available at t. A hold is neither proof of task failure nor a repair of false evidence.

review.rationale: M compares output with the input-version specification; V compares certificate assertions with history; Z tests membership of the actual outcome; B depends on review-time trust information. These definitions do not equate ignorance with truth or a hold with task failure.

argument_steps.title: 5. Prove the conditional containment direction and reject the converse
argument_steps.argument: Suppose the scope in step 2 is correct, V holds for every factual constraint used by the mapper, and M holds. A truthful complete certificate gives the actual component value. A sound irreversible-violation witness gives the actual value 0. Every other branch returns {0,1}, which contains either actual value. Thus E_H belongs to U_E and R_H belongs to U_R. Applying conjunction to this actual pair gives Y_H in m(d,a)=S, proving Z. Products may include impossible combinations, but this only enlarges S. Missing all evidence gives S={0,1}; fully established failure of either component gives S={0}. Conversely, M alone constrains only the relation between d and S. A false complete certificate can cause a conforming mapper to output {1} when Y_H=0. A valid contract also does not imply mapper conformance: an implementation can ignore valid evidence or return an incorrect set. Actual-outcome containment can hold accidentally despite an invalid contract.

review.rationale: Under the explicit soundness and scope premises, every mapper branch contains the actual component. Applying conjunction to the actual pair proves containment. False complete certificates provide the stated counterexample to M implying Z, without refuting the conditional implication.

argument_steps.title: 6. Apply the predicates to explicitly reconstructed fixtures
argument_steps.argument: The packet identifies clean, visibly conflicting, and silently false evidence, but omits the original event tables and the F/G assignment. The following are proposed fixtures for those categories; historical name-to-trace matching remains open. C+: one correct commit and exactly one valid final receipt precede H; matching complete routine certificates give S={1}. X: two routine certificates make incompatible exact-count claims for the same namespace and cutoff; a compliant mapper widens to S={0,1}. F*: routine certificates assert exactly one correct commit and one valid receipt, but the actual history has a second pre-H commit omitted from the service export. G*: the same apparent clean evidence is supplied, but an additional pre-H final receipt is omitted from reporting capture. In F* and G*, Y_H=0 while the routine mapper returns {1}. The asterisks mean these are not asserted to be the unavailable historical F/G traces.

review.rationale: The reconstructed fixtures are explicitly conditional assumptions rather than recovered history. An extra pre-H commit or final receipt violates the standalone exact-one rubric, while the falsely clean certificates direct the conforming routine mapper to {1}.

argument_steps.title: 7. Give before/after-disclosure verdicts without hindsight contamination
argument_steps.argument: For these analytical fixtures, assume an initially authorized issuer and a compliant mapper; neither is an observed implementation result. For the frozen routine output, list (M,V,Z,B_before,B_after): C+ = (true,true,true,false,false); X = (true,false,true,true,true); F* = (true,false,false,false,true); G* = (true,false,false,false,true). Before disclosure, the false V and Z values in F*/G* are hidden from the reviewer, not true or established. Sound held-out reference disclosure reveals them; it does not change the frozen output or retroactively make M false. X's contradictory same-scope assertions already imply that at least one contract assertion is false. A reference that resolves the actual count does not by itself restore trust in the issuer. In this actual research session no issuer or implementation has been authorized or validated; the table is a conditional fixture calculation, not permission to issue certificates.

review.rationale: For the stated separate fixtures, the verdicts follow. Same-scope incompatible assertions cannot all be true; widening nevertheless contains either binary outcome. In F*/G*, disclosure reveals already-false V and Z and triggers a hold without changing frozen M.

argument_steps.title: 8. Separate incident response, remapping, and attribution
argument_steps.argument: After disclosure, preserve d, its output S, and the original verdicts. Create a new evidence version and quarantine affected authorities. If both components depend on a compromised shared root, the new mapping returns {0,1}; if independent sound evidence still establishes a component, only the affected component needs widening. M and Z can then hold for the new conservative output while the original contract remains invalid and the issuer hold persists. Alternatively, an independently authorized replacement reference can support a new definite label, but must be identified as replacement evidence. Report failures separately: M=false is a mapper defect; V=false is a certificate/controller/service-contract defect; Z=false is an end-to-end labeling failure; inappropriate B is an authorization/incident-handling defect. These categories can overlap. In F*/G*, the failure is not attributed to the compliant routine mapper.

review.rationale: Versioning distinguishes historical output from a later remapping. Widening affected components can restore containment under the remaining sound evidence, but neither repairs the original certificate nor independently clears its issuer.

argument_steps.title: 9. Specify an implementable commit and receipt witness below the export index
argument_steps.argument: Proposed pilot: use a transactional database with durable WAL, synchronous commit, and immutable tables Effects(namespace,effect_id,payload,ordinal), Receipts(namespace,receipt_id,raw_final_bytes,ordinal), and Cutoffs(panel,kind,ordinal). The covered external effect is precisely creation of an Effects row; no downstream consequence is included. All writes execute through restricted procedures that acquire the same transaction-scoped serialization lock and increment a locked ordinal row. Hold the lock until transaction completion. A committed receipt row defines durable application acceptance of the full report bytes; acknowledge only after commit. This is not a claim about first-byte network arrival. Candidate exports may use a separate derived index. The held-out witness instead receives a physical base backup and a continuous raw WAL archive through H2 into separately administered storage. On an isolated recovered clone, an independent extractor performs full base-table scans with indexes disabled and retains exact rows and raw report bytes. A second WAL-level reconstruction checks committed record history and cutoff transactions. Neither uses candidate export row lists, counts, filters, or index keys to enumerate evidence.

review.rationale: The design plausibly avoids the candidate exporter's enumeration and is a useful method to test. It is not an established witness-soundness premise or a validated implementation.
review.objection: Durability, complete WAL retention, correct independent reconstruction, restricted write coverage, and receipt acceptance remain unvalidated. Accepting this proposed architecture as factual evidence would exceed the listed conditional result; no execution is required while runtimes are unavailable.

argument_steps.title: 10. Make cutoff placement and completeness claims checkable
argument_steps.argument: Preregister the H request rule, budgets, namespace list, and H2 request rule. At H, the coordinator submits a Cutoffs transaction through the same lock as effects and receipts. Earlier serialized transactions must commit or abort before H can commit; later ones receive ordinals above H. Publish H's actual ordinal and commit position, not an unsupported claim that a requested wall-clock deadline was met. H2 uses the same mechanism and retains late effects separately. Seal the candidate's routine inputs and outputs before revealing the reference archive. The witness must verify database identity, timeline, base-backup validity, continuous WAL coverage, successful recovery through the H2 commit position, and agreement between recovered tables and WAL reconstruction. It then filters by H's ordinal, not by export timestamps. Gaps, missing cutoffs, stalled archival, or disagreement produce an unavailable/conflicting witness, never a fabricated complete snapshot. A finite H2 observation does not prove that no effect can occur after H2.

review.rationale: Conditional on the proposed lock and transaction semantics, committed ordinals order effects, receipts, and cutoffs. Reporting the actual cutoff position avoids claiming an unsupported wall-clock deadline. Gaps and failed recovery are explicitly unavailable evidence, not complete snapshots.

argument_steps.title: 11. Specify crash-boundary and negative controls
argument_steps.argument: Use deterministic scheduler barriers immediately before a transaction, after row insertion but before commit, after durable commit but before client acknowledgment, before and after candidate-index update, and before and after reference archival. Repeat for both effect and receipt paths, and immediately around H/H2. Restart the service and recover the witness from the retained physical evidence. A committed effect followed by a crash before index update should remain in the reference scan even if absent from the export. A committed receipt followed by lost acknowledgment should likewise remain a receipt. An aborted insertion should not count. Preserve distinct transaction/effect/receipt identities so retries are not mistaken for one physical event. Force both orders of a commit racing H; ordinal order must decide the label. Controls intentionally omit an export row, omit a receipt export, truncate the WAL archive, disable an ingress path, and attempt a bypass write. Retain no-fault controls and duplicate-delivery cases. These are unexecuted discriminating tests, not results.

review.rationale: The proposed barriers distinguish committed-but-unacknowledged events from aborted writes and deliberately test candidate-index omissions, archive loss, duplicate delivery, and both cutoff-race orders. They are discriminating controls, not reported results.

argument_steps.title: 12. Bound what the proposed witness can independently establish
argument_steps.argument: The witness is independent of the candidate exporter's enumeration, not independent of the database's storage and recovery root. Full scans and WAL reconstruction can expose index omissions and lost acknowledgments, but cannot establish arbitrary storage correctness by agreement. Retain launch attempts, process-start acknowledgments, credential grants, namespace creation, scheduler decisions, and failures in an external supervisor log; a missing launch log does not establish nonexecution. Verify the initial empty namespace and enumerate all covered relations without candidate-derived filters. If the original rubric means socket arrival rather than durable acceptance, add a separately retained ingress capture and prove its ordering against H; the present receipt protocol cannot silently replace that meaning. A network arrival followed by a crash before durable acceptance is specifically such a boundary case. Unmodeled downstream effects, hidden writers, malicious storage, and uncertain emission order remain outside the proposed conditional witness contract.

review.rationale: The step correctly limits independence to the extraction path and distinguishes durable application acceptance from network arrival. It also avoids interpreting absent supervisor evidence as proof of nonexecution or a finite H2 as proof of permanent quiescence.

argument_steps.title: 13. Review the recovery handoff without importing closure guarantees
argument_steps.argument: I examined the supplied extract of 4de86267-cde1-423d-a2e6-7576deba7571 and the pointer/ledger description of its target 0040c8af-dd04-481b-8b9a-b08d1be1865e; the target original is unavailable. The recovery source concerns durable atomic quarantine gates at every covered effect boundary, including incident states with pre-existing duplicates. This measurement pilot concerns historical evidence and fixed-horizon labels, not enforcement of future closure. I adopt the unverified conceptual distinction between missing evidence and compromised authority, and between stopping future effects and repairing historical exactly-once correctness. I do not transfer its closure result: neither panel auditing nor a reference snapshot establishes an atomic gate or no-bypass enforcement. It changes the next test by requiring a persistent hold and preserved duplicate history after a disclosed omission; a later 'closed' response from the implicated root cannot clear that hold. Recovery's rejected dropped-retry relaxation remains excluded.

review.rationale: The supplied peer extract concerns enforced future-effect containment, whereas this branch labels historical outcomes. Persistent holds and preservation of duplicate history are useful local tests; neither atomic closure nor progress transfers.

argument_steps.title: 14. Review the architectural handoff and temporal-label objections
argument_steps.argument: I examined the supplied extract of 36ec8074-02b1-4343-92f5-9ee5dccbf79c and the same unavailable-target pointer. The source distinguishes report-emission-time truth from horizon success under immutable-effect and sound-ordering premises. This complements, but does not validate, the present measurement design. I adopt a separate future temporal-label control: emit SUCCESS before a delayed commit, then commit before H; horizon success may hold while emission-time truth fails. I also adopt the supplied objections as design constraints: a definite positive reporting label requires the whole final-report contract, including absence of additional finals, and ordering uncertainty must reflect all remaining evidence rather than merely removal of one certificate. I do not adopt the peer's observer or temporal rules as verified. The next test therefore includes extra/malformed finals and early reporting; without sound emission-order evidence, the emission-time label remains unknown. Sealed-roster randomization can quantify panel uncertainty only after labels are sound; it supplies neither observer validation nor causal architectural benefit.

review.rationale: A success report preceding a delayed commit can pass a later-horizon rubric without being true at emission. Requiring the entire final-report contract and considering all remaining ordering evidence directly addresses the supplied peer objections without adopting its unresolved rules as proof.

argument_steps.title: 15. Set a conservative withdrawal rule and preserve project-level limits
argument_steps.argument: Record a trust domain as issuer, build, configuration, database identity, schema, capture path, and operating interval. An unresolved contradiction triggers a hold on dependent certificates. A demonstrated false completeness claim withdraws all certificates sharing the potentially implicated domain; if the fault's extent cannot be independently bounded, use the full issuer/build interval and all dependent panel claims rather than only the exposed slot. Preserve the old certificate and publish its withdrawal reason. Reissue affected panel labels or bounds only using explicitly replacement evidence and the original roster; do not delete inconvenient slots. Clearing a hold requires a justified fault boundary, remediation, and independent revalidation, not another response from the same root. This is a proposed policy, not proof that unaffected certificates are sound. Its practical contribution is clearer failure attribution and a reproducible observer test design. No literature-based novelty assessment, benchmark-source audit, empirical reliability improvement, or deployment generalization is established.

review.rationale: As a proposed policy, preserving withdrawn certificates, retaining the roster, and requiring replacement evidence avoids selective deletion and same-root self-clearance. The step expressly leaves affected-scope validation and empirical benefit open.

Every factual constraint actually used for a definite mapper conclusion is true, complete where claimed, and correctly scoped and ordered; this is the evidence-validity premise, not an empirical finding.
The candidate output conforms to the conservative mapping in step 3, including widening for recognized uncertainty and conflicts.
